procedural_matters: The panel of the international jury was composed in accordance with RRS N1.4(b).
GER 3356 was represented by Antonia Schwarz.
SGP 3562 was represented by Sean Kum.

Protest time limit for emerald fleet on 8th July was at 15:51. GER 3356 waited in line in the harbour to get back ashore and after arriving ashore she immediately submitted the protest at 15:53. GER 3356 failed to deliver the protest within the protest time limit, as required by RRS 60.3(b)(1). However, there was good reason for the international jury to extend the time limit. Therefore the protest is valid under RRS 60.4(1)(a).
facts: Race F2, emerald fleet, leg 2, conditions: 15 knots
GER 3356 and SGP 3562 overlapped sailing downwind course on a starboard tack.
GER 3356 windward of SGP 3562, with a distance between them less than 1,5 boat lengths.
SGP 3562 slightly luffed, GER 3356 held her course.
GER 3356 was sailing faster than SGP 3562. When SGP 3562 got blanketed by GER 3356, he rapidly heeled to windward and contact occurred between SGP 3562's mast and GER 3356's top part of main sail.
There is a damage to GER 3356 boat, 30 cm hole in the top part of the main sail.
conclusions: When changing course SGP 3562 the right-of-way boat gave GER 3356 room to keep clear, and complied with RRS 16.1.
GER 3356 to windward failed to keep clear of SGP 3562 to leeward, and broke RRS 11.
GER 3356 did not avoid contact with SGP 3562 even though it was reasonably possible, and broke RRS 14(a).
It was not reasonably possible for SGP 3562 the right-of-way boat to avoid contact with GER 3356 when it became clear that GER 3356 was not keeping clear. SGP 3562 did not break RRS 14(a).
GER 3356’s score in race F2 was made significantly worse through her own fault. Therefore, the requirements for redress in RRS 61.4(b) are not met.
decision: GER 3356 is DSQ in race F2.
